why: A has three conjuncts. not_theorem_10_5_7 says the project's transcription Theorem_10_5_7 (universe 0, with the project's EpStrongBundle.IsLR) is false. isLR_z3EpBundle says the trivial bundle ℝ × ℝᵏ → ℝ over ℤ/3 × ℝ ⇉ ℝ (trivial μ) has that (LR). remark_10_5_5 says [W ←1 W →Inv W] and [1_W] are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with the same orbit map that differ, already on the bases. B is Theorem 10.5.7 read literally, with the blind author's IsLRB (Definition 8.4.2 tested on all strong bundle isomorphisms of W|U(x)). As its author predicted, B does not hold as we read it. not_B (rt_check OK) re-does the project's counterexample from non-item lemmas. z3SEP 0 has IsLRB: μ is the projection, so an orbit-preserving Φ is the identity, which is the natural lift of 1. The two classes are separated by the isotropy relation at the generator of ℤ/3 (isotropyRel_id, not_isotropyRel_inv, Diagram.Equiv.isotropyRel_iff). Hence A ⇒ B is false (not_A_to_B), and B ⇒ A holds only ex falso. A_to_notB (rt_check OK, uses A) shows that A's own counterexample also refutes B, since it satisfies B's stronger-looking (LR). So the two sides agree that the text's claim fails, and on why. The IsLRB/IsLR difference the blind author flagged does not matter here.
